title: Enable gh API request logging in bot workflow steps with GH_DEBUG=api
answers: How do I log gh API requests in a GitHub Actions step?
How to debug duplicate labels or duplicate events from gh pr create or gh pr edit in CI
Turn on verbose gh api debug output in a workflow
gh GH_DEBUG api environment variable in workflow
body:
To see the HTTP requests a `gh` command makes in a workflow step, set `GH_DEBUG: api` in that step's `env:` block, next to `GH_TOKEN`.
The PR set it on the bot PR-creation steps in `.github/workflows/update-model-catalog.yml` (step id `pr`) and `.github/workflows/uv.yml` (the step that runs `gh pr create`), with a comment saying it was for diagnosing labels applied twice.
It is set per step, so it logs only that step's `gh` calls and does not affect the rest of the job.
The log goes to the step output, so read it from the Actions run log for that step.
The PR's stated purpose was to tell client-side duplication from server-side duplication. It does not show what the logs revealed.
Remove the variable when the diagnosis is finished, unless the log volume is acceptable to keep.
applies: Diagnostic use in GitHub Actions steps that call the gh CLI; not a fix for duplicate label events by itself.
says: Automated pull request creation bot is applying duplicate labels to new pull requests.
Enable detailed request logging in workflow runs to diagnose automated pull request actions.
Workflow bots generate duplicated label events whenever publishing automated repository update requests.
How can we check whether duplicate pull request tags come from clients or servers?
Inspect raw API traffic in build logs to troubleshoot bot pull request operations.
